newsitem.title: USA: Bees to hit five-year high.
newsitem.headline: Bees to hit five-year high.

text.p: Despite the onslaught of action films hitting movie theatres in the coming weeks, this summer might just be the time for a rerelease of "The Swarm," a 1970s box office bomb about killer bees.
Bee experts predict that the nasty stinging critters will be crashing more than their usual share of summer cookouts and ballgames.

Jim Abraham, owner of Bee Control, a Pittsburgh-based company specialising in the control of stinging insects, predicts this summer's bee and wasp population, especially across the mid-Atlantic region, will buzz to an all-time high.

"The '97 season from April through October will go down in the record books due to the extremely mild winter," he said. "But I wouldn't advise anyone to curtail their outdoor summer activities. Just expect to see more bee and wasp activity."

Abraham, who removes bee and wasp nests from homes and businesses, said he already has handled a record number of service requests this year. Bee and wasp populations are up because the mild winter did not kill many hibernating queens.

"Cold temperatures are the biggest killer of queens, who create the nests," he said. "The population peaks every three, four or five years. We were due for a peak, but concurrent with the mild winter the population will be the worst in at least the last five years."
The best advice to avoid being stung? Stand still when a bee or wasp is flying near you. Do not drink sweet-smelling soda from a can. And avoid sweet-smelling perfumes and hairsprays.
You can also pour ammonia around your cookout site because the smell repels stinging insects, Abraham said, although it might also repel your guests.
If all else fails, go to the movies. There are killer planes, cruise ships and terrorists on the loose -- but, at least so far this season, no bees.
